metadata.title: Walmart downgraded, Palantir upgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
Deutsche Bank upgraded Palantir (PLTR) to Buy from Hold with an unchanged price target of $200. The firm views the company's Q2 report as "exceptional."
-
Oppenheimer upgraded Inspire Medical (INSP) to Outperform from Perform with an $85 price target. The firm notes the company's Q2 revenues of $201M slightly outpaced estimates, and argues that at these levels, there is "noisy" value to the story as a mid to high single digit grower.
-
UBS upgraded BBB Foods (TBBB) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $51, up from $43. The company has delivered same-store-sales well ahead of inflation and its business benefits from consumers seeking value, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
Leerink upgraded Replimune (REPL) to Outperform from Market Perform with a price target of $17, up from $11. The firm has "high conviction" the FDA will grant RP-1 plus nivolumab accelerated approval.
-
Wolfe Research upgraded Madrigal Pharmaceuticals (MDGL) to Outperform from Peer Perform with a $605 price target. The firm says the shares overcorrected on perception of its stage 4 liver fibrosis data coming late or being delayed.
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
Oppenheimer downgraded Walmart (WMT) to Perform from Outperform without a price target ahead of the earnings report on August 20. The firm sees a "less compelling outperformance case" for the shares in the near-term.
-
China Renaissance downgraded Apple (AAPL) to Hold from Buy with a $280 price target after the company reported in line Q3 results and issued Q4 guidance that missed expectations.
-
Citizens downgraded eBay (EBAY) to Market Perform from Outperform without a price target. The firm believes consensus estimates for the company are too high.
-
JPMorgan downgraded Nike (NKE) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $40, down from $47. Nike's "Win Now" decisions made in 2026 will hurt profits into the fiscal 2028, the firm tells investors in a research note. JPMorgan also downgraded PVH Corp. (PVH) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $84, up from $70.
-
Jefferies downgraded Cigna (CI) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $307, down from $336. The firm believes consensus estimates for Cigna look a "little high" with the EviCore sale and Centene prescription drug plan shrinkage as potential negatives.
Top 5 Initiations:
-
Piper Sandler initiated coverage of CoreWeave (CRWV) with an Overweight rating and $151 price target. Piper has a favorable view of the public neocloud industry and believes CoreWeave's engineering team provides differentiation that can reduce costs. Piper Sandler also started coverage of Nebius (NBIS) but with a Neutral rating and $224 price target. Piper has a favorable view of the public neocloud industry.
-
Cantor Fitzgerald initiated coverage of SK Hynix (SKHY) with an Overweight rating and $300 price target, which represents 100% upside from current levels. Cantor sees sustained growth in revenue, margins, and free cash flow for both Hynix and the memory industry, led by continued price increases and migrations to higher value solutions. Needham, Wolfe Research, William Blair, RBC Capital, and Rosenblatt also started coverage of SK Hynix with Buy-equivalent ratings.
-
Loop Capital initiated coverage of Rubrik (RBRK) with a Buy rating and $100 price target. Cyber resilience is emerging as a "major secular growth" opportunity and Rubrik is among the best positioned vendors to benefit, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
DA Davidson initiated coverage of SailPoint (SAIL) with a Neutral rating and $17 price target. SailPoint "remains the clear market leader" in Identity Governance and Administration, but total ARR growth and SaaS ARR growth as reported and ex-migrations have been decelerating, says the firm, which recommend waiting for a more attractive entry point or more signs of NNARR acceleration.
-
Roth Capital initiated coverage of Arteris (AIP) with a Buy rating and $40 price target. The firm believes the company's interconnect IP and automation software solutions can grow with increasing data movement demands.
